meaning: to have to start planning something again from the beginning because the first attempt failed
literal_translation: Zacząć wszystko od nowa, bo poprzedni plan się nie udał i trzeba wrócić do projektowania
example: The first prototype of the gene-editing tool failed the safety tests, so the team had to go back to the drawing board.
origin: Comes from engineering and architecture, where designers return to their drawing boards to revise plans after a design is rejected; the phrase has been used in English since the mid-20th century

wrong_meanings.meaning: to draw pictures for pleasure during a break
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is not about drawing as a hobby; it describes restarting a plan after a failure

wrong_meanings.meaning: to buy new art supplies for a studio
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with shopping; it refers to revising a plan from the beginning

wrong_meanings.meaning: to finish a project quickly without changes
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which describes starting again because the earlier version was not successful

explanation: 'Back to the drawing board' means that an idea or plan has not worked, so the people involved must start planning again from the beginning. It is often used in discussions of science and technology, when a new approach must be designed after a test or experiment has failed.
